⏺ A watch-only wallet lets users monitor balances and transactions without holding private keys
⏺ This setup is useful for large portfolios, cold storage, and address analysis
⏺ This post explains why monitoring assets doesn't require spending access

1️⃣ Core Idea — the app receives a public wallet address and displays its assets and transaction history.
2️⃣ Why It Helps — users can monitor long-term holdings without connecting the device that stores their private keys.
3️⃣ Use Cases — cold wallets, corporate treasuries, whale monitoring, and crypto portfolio accounting.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — the app cannot sign transactions without a key, but it may collect information about your addresses and financial activity.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — add only public addresses, verify supported networks, and never enter a seed phrase just to view balances.


Final Thoughts

You don't need to give an app control over your crypto just to monitor it. Separating viewing from signing reduces situations where private keys are exposed to unnecessary risk.

Brussels Pulls the Plug on Canada’s EU Membership Dream 🇨🇦🇪🇺

The European Union is backing away from a controversial proposal to make Canada its first “associate member,” after resistance from several key member states threatened to derail the initiative ahead of a major summit in Montreal.

European Commission President Von der Leyen floated the idea in September, presenting it as a way to deepen ties with Ottawa amid growing geopolitical uncertainty and strained relations between Canada and the United States under Trump.

But Germany, France, Italy and Greece raised objections, arguing that associate membership has no clear legal basis in EU treaties and could create confusion about the bloc’s future relationships with other countries seeking closer ties to Europe.

The disagreement has forced Brussels and Ottawa to reconsider the wording of their joint declaration. Instead of explicitly referring to associate membership, the draft now calls for an “ever closer association” between Canada and the EU, with negotiations expected to continue until next year’s summit. 

For Canadian Prime Minister Carney, strengthening ties with Europe is part of a broader strategy to reduce his country’s dependence on the United States. Washington remains Canada’s dominant trading partner, leaving Ottawa vulnerable to tariffs and political pressure from the Trump administration.

Closer cooperation with Europe could open new opportunities in trade, defense, energy, critical minerals, artificial intelligence and digital technology. Both sides also see potential for stronger economic and security partnerships as global competition intensifies. 

Despite the setback, the proposal has not ended the push for closer relations. Canadian officials have emphasized that the substance of the partnership matters more than its formal title, while European governments broadly support expanding cooperation.

The dispute, however, exposes divisions within the EU over how far the bloc should go in developing new forms of partnership beyond full membership. For now, Brussels appears determined to pursue closer ties with Canada without committing to a status that remains legally undefined.

🔖 Australia proposes new crypto exchange rules for 2027 

📣 Australia has proposed new rules for cryptocurrency trading and custody platforms on October 15, 2026, with financial regulator ASIC seeking public feedback by November 27 before the country’s digital asset licensing framework takes effect in April 2027. 

📊 The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) announced the consultation alongside Consultation Paper 392, which outlines planned requirements for customer asset protection, trading practices and financial resources. The regulator expects to publish final guidance in March 2027, giving businesses time to prepare for the new licensing requirements. Australia’s upcoming rules will bring more cryptocurrency businesses under the country’s existing financial services licensing framework.

⚡️ The Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 creates two regulated categories: digital asset platforms and tokenized custody platforms. Digital asset platforms hold digital tokens for customers and provide related services, while tokenized custody platforms use digital tokens to record customers’ rights to underlying assets.
